definitions.explanation: Sake specifically intended for cooking rather than drinking. Used to remove odors from meat and fish, add flavor, and tenderize ingredients.

examples.japanese: {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}を{大|おお}さじ{一杯|いっぱい}{加|くわ}える。
examples.english: Add one tablespoon of cooking sake.

examples.japanese: {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}は{肉|にく}や{魚|さかな}の{臭|くさ}みを{取|と}るのに{使|つか}う。
examples.english: Cooking sake is used to remove the odor from meat and fish.

examples.japanese: {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}がないときは{普通|ふつう}の{日本酒|にほんしゅ}で{代用|だいよう}できる。
examples.english: When you don't have cooking sake, you can substitute regular sake.

notes:
USAGE:
A staple seasoning in Japanese cooking alongside {醤油|しょうゆ} (soy sauce) and {味醂|みりん} (sweet rice wine). {料理酒|りょうりしゅ} typically has salt added to make it undrinkable, which classifies it as a seasoning rather than an alcoholic beverage in Japan. This allows it to be sold without a liquor license.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}を{加|くわ}える (to add cooking sake)
- {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}で{下味|したあじ}をつける (to season with cooking sake)
- {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}と{醤油|しょうゆ} (cooking sake and soy sauce)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {味醂|みりん}: mirin, sweet rice wine — sweeter, used for glazing and sweetening
- {日本酒|にほんしゅ}: sake — drinking sake, can also be used for cooking
